travelAdvisory.summary:
Updated to reflect a shift to Level 2 “Exercise increased caution” for Mainland China.
Summary: Exercise increased caution when traveling to Mainland China due to arbitrary enforcement of local laws, including in relation to exit bans.
Exercise increased caution when traveling to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) due to the arbitrary enforcement of local laws.
Reconsider travel to the Macau Special Administrative Region (SAR) due to a limited ability to provide emergency consular

medications.generalAdvice: China has extremely strict narcotics laws. ANY amount of many substances triggers severe criminal penalties. Carry only essential medications with official Chinese-translated prescriptions and doctor letters. Do NOT bring opioids, psychotropics, or stimulants without advance NMPA approval.

controlledSubstances.note: Zero tolerance. Even trace amounts can lead to arrest and imprisonment. CBD products also prohibited.
Strictly prohibited. No import exemption. Carrying results in criminal prosecution.
Prohibited without advance NMPA (National Medical Products Administration) approval, which is rarely granted to tourists.
Requires advance approval from NMPA. Carry original prescription with Chinese translation. Strictly limit to personal use quantities.
Carry original prescription with official Chinese translation. Declare at customs. Maximum 1-month supply.

scams.name: Tea House Scam
scams.description: Friendly locals invite you to a tea ceremony, then you're pressured into paying an enormous bill.
scams.avoidance: Decline invitations from strangers. Check prices before ordering.

scams.name: Black Taxi Scam
scams.description: Unlicensed taxis at airports charge 5-10x normal fares.
scams.avoidance: Use official taxi queues or DiDi app. Insist on the meter.

scams.name: Fake Monk Blessing
scams.description: People dressed as monks give you a bracelet then aggressively demand 100-500 yuan.
scams.avoidance: Real monks don't solicit on the street. Don't accept items handed to you.

scams.name: Art Student Scam
scams.description: Young people invite you to their art exhibition and pressure you to buy overpriced artwork.
scams.avoidance: Decline street invitations. Visit established galleries independently.

connectivity.simOptions: Foreign SIM cards and eSIMs work for calls/data but cannot access Google, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp without VPN. China Unicom or China Mobile tourist SIMs at airports.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at hotels, cafes, and airports but often requires Chinese phone number for registration. Many Western services are blocked.
connectivity.bestOption: Get a VPN before arriving (download in advance — VPN apps blocked in China). eSIM with roaming from Airalo or Holafly bypasses the firewall via foreign routing.

cultural.tipping: Not expected and not customary. Some high-end international hotels may accept tips. Taxi drivers do not expect tips.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress at temples and religious sites. Cover shoulders and knees. Business settings are formal. Casual dress is fine in cities.
cultural.greetings: Handshake is common in business. Slight nod for casual greetings. Address people by title + surname. Business cards exchanged with both hands.
taboos: Sticking chopsticks upright in rice (funeral symbolism)
Writing names in red ink (associated with death)
Giving clocks as gifts (sounds like 'attending a funeral')
Discussing Taiwan, Tibet, or Tiananmen Square politics
cultural.haggling: Expected at markets, street vendors, and some small shops. Not at department stores, malls, or restaurants. Start at 30-50% of asking price.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: visa required. Transit visa-free for 144h in select cities. Most Western nationals need a visa.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: March-May (spring) and September-November (autumn). Avoid Chinese New Year (late Jan/Feb) and Golden Week (Oct 1-7) — extreme crowds.

immediate: Drop, cover, and hold on under sturdy desk or against interior wall
Stay away from windows and heavy shelving
Move away from buildings if outdoors — China has active seismic zones
Do not use elevators after shaking
after: Follow instructions from local government and police
Contact US Embassy or Consulate if assistance needed

immediate: Monitor China Meteorological Administration (CMA) typhoon warnings
Stay indoors when Yellow/Orange/Red typhoon signal issued
Secure loose outdoor items and stay away from coastal areas
after: Watch for flooding and landslides following typhoon passage
Check roads before traveling in affected areas

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 110)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (110) and ambulance (120) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the RIGHT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
